PQC R2 kill-test at REAL 576-MTU fragmentation (CREATE_CHILD path): veth MTU 576 fragments the CREATE_CHILD rekey request/response + IKE_FOLLOWUP_KE ML-KEM exchange; netem 30% then 5% on responder->initiator across the 60s-soft rekey (80% blows the 10s ADDKE arm timer before FOLLOWUP install); counted-drop gate (netem-dropped >= 1 AND R2 replay >= 1 AND SKF fragment recv >= 3 AND a new g_ir_present=Y keymat), responder holds its SA (3600s) so only the initiator rekeys; i2iinit-drop576 proves the IKE_INTERMEDIATE fragment path only, not CREATE_CHILD fragment replay. CREATECHILD mid-handler duplicate unit (review #5): netem duplicate 100% on the INITIATOR egress veth after child-up, so the rekey CREATE_CHILD REQUEST arrives twice back-to-back.  Dispatch (ikev2.c:538) short-circuits the second copy BEFORE the handler: pre-arm -> check_message_ordering sees recv_message_id advanced -> dropping-unordered; post-arm -> R2 replay.  Gate: exactly ONE 'CREATE_CHILD_SA request' handler entry (resp log, scoped to the rekey msgid) AND rekey completes (new SPI both sides) AND no abort AND (marker lines unordered+R2replay+frag-drop >= 1 OR a tcpdump -X msgid scan counts >= 2 msgid-M request packets on the responder-ingress tap — the wire count is the direct duplicate-arrival measurement and substitutes when the pre-arm drop path stays silent; box 2026-09-26 proved markers can be 0 with a completed rekey).  Two handler entries = the window hole is real.  Classical ESP (no ADDKE followup): the reassembler stores SKF fragments unconditionally (ikev2_frag.c:765) with a count-based completion (:778), so a duplicated mid-list fragment livelocks assembly and an ADDKE dup row would fail for the wrong reason.  DPD/NAT-D reply path unreachable (no yield between advance and arm) — documented, not a row.  gate=box: box-only until a container run passes.

PQC REQUEST-direction loss kill-test (review #4): every existing loss row drops responder->initiator only.  This row nets the INITIATOR egress veth (100% loss KEPT until the netem drop counter ticks — the counted loss of the first request copy — held ~4s so the 1s/3s ladder rungs are counted too, then qdisc REMOVED so the 7s rung arrives and FOLLOWUP+response ride the 10s ADDKE arm timer clean; dpd_delay 60 cannot pollute the window: earliest initiator DPD leaves after the qdisc is gone); recovery is the INITIATOR's own retransmit ladder (1,2,4,8...s), not a responder replay — no R2 replay expected or required.  Gate: counted netem-dropped >= 1 on the REQUEST direction AND the request logged strictly AFTER qdisc removal AND rekey completes (new SPI both sides) AND the NEW keymat carries g_ir_present=Y on BOTH sides with matching sha256 AND no followup timeout.  Completion with zero counted request loss proves nothing.  gate=box: box-only until a container run passes.
